claims.voice_position: Tanwir report, Ibn Abbas attribution disputed
claims.statement_en: The abundance is explained as abundant good, with the Quran included within it.

claims.voice_position: alternative Tanwir gloss, Ibn Abbas attribution disputed
claims.statement_en: An alternative identifies al-Kawthar as a river in Paradise given to Muhammad.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: ويقال الكوثر نهر فى الجنة أعطاه الله محمدا

claims.voice_position: Tanwir alternative glosses, Ibn Abbas attribution disputed
claims.statement_en: Wanhar is explained as facing the qibla with the chest, or placing the right hand over the left during prayer.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: استقبل بنحرك إلى القبلة ويقال ضع يمينك على شمالك في الصلاة

claims.voice_position: Tanwir alternative gloss, Ibn Abbas attribution disputed
claims.statement_en: Another explanation is to complete bowing and prostration until the chest becomes visible.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: استوف الركوع والسجود حتى يبدو نحرك

claims.voice_position: Tanwir alternative gloss, Ibn Abbas attribution disputed
claims.statement_en: Another explanation directs prayer on the Day of Sacrifice and the slaughter of sacrificial camels.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: صل لربك صلاة يوم النحر وانحر البدن

claims.voice_position: Tanwir lexical and consequence gloss, Ibn Abbas attribution disputed
claims.statement_en: The hater is described as cut off from family, children, wealth, and every good, and as not remembered well after death.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: مبغضك ... أبتر عن أهله وولده وماله وعن كل خير لا يذكر بعد موته بخير

claims.voice_position: Tanwir occasion identification, Ibn Abbas attribution disputed
claims.statement_en: The hostile referent is identified as al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi; the report contrasts his fate with Muhammad's favorable remembrance and relates the insult to the death of Muhammad's son Abdullah.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: وهو العاص بن وائل السهمي ... مات ابنه عبد الله
